name: Estonian Setu leelo polyphonic song
lineage: Estonian Setu leelo polyphonic women's-song tradition of the Setu region (southeast Estonia and adjacent Pechory district of Russia). The Setu are a distinct Estonian-and-Russian-borderland Finno-Ugric ethnic group whose linguistic-cultural identity preserves archaic Finno-Ugric features lost in mainstream Estonian. Leelo is performed by a women's group with the lead singer (sõnoline, "the word-singer") improvising the verse text and melodic line, answered by the choral group (torrõ, "the resonators") in unison or in a sustained drone-bourdon below the melodic line. The drone configuration distinguishes leelo from neighboring Baltic polyphonic traditions: the torrõ chorus holds a sustained pedal-tone while the sõnoline elaborates above, producing a drone-and-melodic-elaboration register more akin to certain Slavic and Central-Asian traditions than to the parallel-second sutartinė style. Vocabulary draws on a regional Estonian-Setu pentatonic-leaning modal system. Verse-form is Kalevala-meter (the canonical Finno-Ugric four-stress eight-syllable line shared with the Finnish-Karelian Kalevala epic). Repertoire spans calendar-rite celebrations, wedding-cycle songs (Setu weddings featured the most elaborated leelo repertoire, with sung-confrontation-and-praise sequences between bride-and-groom parties), funeral-lament cycles, and the contemporary Värska-Obinitsa Setu cultural-festival circuit. Mipu Music MIPUCD 104 — Setusongs (1991, recorded May 1990) provides the canonical Western-distributed documentation. Distinguished from Lithuanian sutartinės by Setu leelo's drone-and-melody (vs Lithuanian parallel-seconds) configuration; distinguished from Karelian rune-singing by Setu's antiphonal-with-drone (vs Karelian's strict-alternation) architecture; distinguished from mainland Estonian regilaul by Setu-dialect-specific vocabulary and Estonian-Russian-borderland regional context.
